correctness.rationale: The full-square max proof is an affine-in-product exact reduction plus exhaustive boundary and diagonal comparisons. The positive stationary cubic value decreases strictly and has one algebraic crossing. Both spinodals have analytically checked derivatives/Hessian and equality-case paths, with microscopic rates chosen nonnegative for all parameters. The standalone test reproduces 181403 assertions, not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A source-exact stationary cubic is unequivocally prior. The precise independent-density global maximizer allocation, algebraic switch and two local-threshold classifications were not located in the inspected primary material or published-result searches; different lane-changing flux-shape theorems are scientifically inapplicable, as detailed. The result is a derived optimization of older flux, not mathematically independent, and uninspected parts or unindexed general theory impose residual risk.
residual_risks: The claim is a mathematically natural optimization of an already known polynomial. A prior general extremum theorem may subsume it without matching the title or decimal constants.
Some plausible older multilane papers were examined in relevant sections, not page-by-page in full.

value.rationale: The exact optimal total stationary throughput is the naturally measurable transport-capacity design objective for two independently loaded coupled lanes. A complete discontinuous allocation classification and two distinct stability boundaries describe when balanced flow becomes inferior to idling one lane. This is structurally motivated and meaningful in the family of models with rigorously known stationary measures, rather than a table lookup or isolated finite sample.
